answer: At the dawn of each epoch, our network enforces topological cut verifications across the trust graph. Multi-agent auditing audits each sparse cut, requiring nodes to stake funds. If clustered identities form an isolated nebula or attempt a bridge exploit like a false jetty, cross-auditors trigger stake slashing. This game-theoretic penalty scales superlinear attacker cost with each fabricated identity, making coordinated Sybils economically unviable.
